# Security Policy

## Supported versions

Security fixes are applied on the latest release of Arrmada only.

| Version | Supported |
| ------- | --------- |
| Latest release | Yes |
| Older releases | No |

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please **do not** open a public GitHub issue for security problems
(leaked keys, auth bypass, unsafe handling of credentials, etc.).

### Preferred: private report on GitHub

Use GitHub’s private vulnerability reporting:

1. Open [Security → Advisories](https://github.com/R0binT/Arrmada/security/advisories) on this repository.
2. Click **Report a vulnerability**.
3. Describe the issue, impact, and steps to reproduce (as much as you can).

We will acknowledge the report when we can and follow up privately through
GitHub. If we accept the report, we may publish a security advisory after a
fix is available. If we decline it, we will explain why.

### What to include

- What is affected (screen, API call, storage, build, dependency, …)
- How severe you think it is
- Steps to reproduce
- Any proof-of-concept (without sharing real secrets)

### Out of scope (examples)

- Issues that only affect your own Radarr/Sonarr servers or LAN setup
- Feature requests that are not security bugs
- Reports that require publishing real API keys or personal data

Thank you for helping keep Arrmada and its users safer.
